newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ex-Bank of Israel chief Bruno dies at 64.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Bank of Israel chief Bruno dies at 64.

text.p: Michael Bruno, a former Bank of Israel governor credited with helping to stabilise the Israeli economy, died on Wednesday night of an illness at the age of 64, the Hebrew University said on Thursday.
Bruno, who was vice president and chief economist at the World Bank until a few months ago, was governor of the Bank of Israel from 1986 to 1991. He was a member of the university faculty.
He helped to stabilise Israel's economy after a period of hyperinflation and laid the groundwork for the economy's rapid growth in the 1990s.
In one of his last public statements, in November, Bruno assailed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for failing to carry through on promises to cut the budget and liberalise the economy.
"What stands out in the economy in these 180 days...is that there is talk, talk and more talk but nothing is being done," he said, referring to the first six months of Netanyahu's term.
Bruno praised the economic impact of the Middle East peace process but said that the current government could upset it.

"There is one very good legacy left by the former government and that is the peace process, which had a very positive projection on the economic realm," he said. "I have a serious suspicion from what I see and hear that this legacy could be spoiled."

Born in Hamburg, Germany, in 1932, Bruno arrived in what was then Palestine with his family a year later. He received degrees from Cambridge and Stanford universities and began teaching at the Hebrew University in 1963. He joined the Bank of Israel in 1974 as head of research.
Bruno won the Israel Prize in 1994 and advised the governments of Mexico, Yugoslavia and Poland on economic policy.
